text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after surging 21% over the prior week, as the stock gave back some gains amid conflicting signals for refiners. The biggest headwind is the Trump-Putin diesel deal announced today—Russian diesel flooding U.S. and global markets would directly undercut refiner margins (the profit spread between crude costs and product prices), since refineries like Marathon make money partly by turning crude into diesel. That deal offsets some of the positive momentum from earlier in the week when oil prices jumped on Middle East tensions and Hurricane Isaias threatened Gulf production.

The broader picture is tangled. Oil prices remain well above $96 per barrel, refineries are running hot at 92.7%, and geopolitical risks from Iran-backed attacks and Saudi tensions should keep crude elevated—all normally supportive for refiners. But the Putin deal is a concrete, near-term margin threat, and it arrived as the stock had already run up sharply, likely prompting some profit-taking or recalibration of the near-term outlook.
